summary.oneLiner: Angel Fibers Limited is a Gujarat-based single-product cotton-yarn spinner operating an aggregate installed capacity of 39,648 spindles.
summary.business: The Company is principally engaged in the manufacture and marketing of cotton yarn. Its spinning units are situated between Rajkot and Jamnagar, a prominent cotton-producing region in Gujarat, with an aggregate installed capacity of 39,648 spindles. The Company is engaged in manufacturing of only one product, i.e. cotton yarn, and hence reports a single segment; the secretarial auditor describes the business as manufacturing of varied cotton yarn from raw cotton.

Textiles (single segment): Cotton yarn (varied counts, spun from raw cotton)

endMarkets: Domestic cotton-yarn demand from downstream garments, hosiery, fabrics and home textiles|Export markets (the Company reported foreign exchange earnings and foreign exchange expenditure of Rs. 4,71,45,463 during the year)

currentContext.strengths: Spinning units located between Rajkot and Jamnagar in a prominent cotton-producing region of Gujarat, giving proximity to raw cotton|Access to a same-line-of-business related party (Murlidhar Worldtrade Private Limited, manufacturing of cotton yarn) that can cover any shortfall in raw materials or finished goods and enable timely supply, supporting business continuity|Improving balance-sheet position: finance cost of the company declined by approximately 27% and the debt-equity ratio fell to 1.18 from 1.59 due to repayment of debt during the year, with interest coverage improving to 2.73 times|Cost-audited, single-product operations with a stated internal control framework reviewed periodically by an independent internal audit team and the Audit Committee
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen cost efficiencies and optimise the supply chain in order to improve margins in the coming years, after a year in which margin fluctuation caused a decline in profitability despite turnover growth (Chairman's message).|Continue deleveraging and prudent financial management: finance cost declined by approximately 27% and the debt-equity ratio fell to 1.18 from 1.59 on repayment of debt, with the Company stating it maintains healthy cash flows sufficient to meet all interest and debt obligations on time.|Conserve funds internally rather than distribute them - the Board did not recommend a dividend for FY 2025-26 in order to conserve funds.|Remain a single-product cotton-yarn spinner: the Company operates one segment, imported no technology during the year and incurred no research and development expenditure.|Control energy cost through strict day-to-day monitoring of power consumption to ensure optimal use of energy with minimum possible wastage.|Secure raw-material and finished-goods continuity through arrangements with same-line-of-business related parties, for which omnibus material RPT approval of up to Rs. 100 crore each is being sought for FY 2026-27, on the stated logic that the related party can cover any shortfall in raw materials or finished goods and enable the Company to meet customer requirements without delay.
currentContext.expansion: The annual report discloses no capex, capacity-addition or expansion project. The only capacity statement is the existing footprint: the Company's spinning units are situated between Rajkot and Jamnagar, a prominent cotton-producing region in Gujarat, with an aggregate installed capacity of 39,648 spindles, operated from a single unit at Survey No. 100/1, Plot No. 1, Kalavad-Ranuja Road, Haripar, Tal. Kalavad, Dist. Jamnagar. No commissioning, ramp-up, debottlenecking, new-site or acquisition language appears anywhere in the routed text. The Directors' Report states there was no material change or commitment during the year under review, that the Company has not imported any technology and that no expenditure was incurred on research and development. Capital deployment during the year ran the other way: the Board conserved funds by not recommending a dividend, and debt was repaid, taking the debt-equity ratio to 1.18 from 1.59 and cutting finance cost by approximately 27%. The MD&A notes, as an industry-level opportunity rather than a company plan, that investment in automation, energy-efficient machinery and improved process controls offers scope for higher productivity and lower manufacturing costs.
currentContext.mdna: Outlook for the spinning industry is described as cautiously positive, supported by India's established cotton base, the integrated textile value chain and continuing domestic demand for yarn.|Cotton yarn, fabrics and made-up textile exports recorded growth of approximately 4.1% in November 2025, which management reads as an improvement in demand during the period.|Growth in domestic garments, hosiery, fabrics and home textiles is expected to support demand for quality cotton yarn.|Diversification of global sourcing may create additional export opportunities for efficient and quality-focused Indian spinning mills.|Demand for compact, contamination-controlled, organic and sustainably produced yarn provides scope for product diversification and improved realisations.|Investment in automation, energy-efficient machinery and improved process controls offers scope for higher productivity and lower manufacturing costs.|Policy support is cited as a driver: the Ministry of Textiles target of textile and apparel exports of Rs. 9 lakh crore by 2030, seven PM MITRA Parks with an approved outlay of Rs. 4,445 crore expected to improve infrastructure and reduce logistics costs, and a 19% increase in the Ministry's Union Budget allocation to Rs. 5,272 crore for FY 2025-26.|Raw-material availability was aided by the Government temporarily exempting all varieties of imported cotton from the applicable 11% import duty up to 31 December 2025, with the objective of improving availability and stabilising input costs.|Management states that future performance will remain dependent on cotton availability and prices, yarn realisations, energy costs, capacity utilisation and demand conditions in domestic and international markets.|Spinning units with efficient cotton procurement, consistent quality and diversified domestic and export customers are expected to be better positioned to benefit.

risks.risk: Cotton price, availability and quality volatility (with exchange-rate movement)
risks.note: MD&A Risks and Concerns states that fluctuations in cotton prices, availability, quality and exchange rates may materially affect production costs, inventory values and profitability; the Threats section adds that volatility in domestic and international cotton prices may adversely affect raw-material costs, inventory valuation and operating margins. For a pure spinner, cotton is the dominant cost line and the pass-through to yarn realisations is not automatic - the Chairman attributes the year's fall in profitability to fluctuation in profit margins despite turnover growth.

risks.risk: Dependence on seasonal cotton arrivals - procurement, inventory and working-capital risk
risks.note: The Company states that dependence on seasonal cotton procurement exposes it to supply-chain disruption, stock-holding and price-mismatch risks, and that seasonal arrivals may result in higher working-capital requirements. This is structural for a mill that must build cotton stock in the arrival season and carry it, and it showed up in the year: inventory holding days rose from 36.28 days to 40.92 days and the inventory turnover ratio fell to 8.92 times from 10.06 times.

risks.risk: Export demand and global tariff uncertainty compressing yarn realisations
risks.note: MD&A flags that uncertainty arising from global tariffs and changing international demand may impact cotton-yarn exports and selling prices, and that global tariff-related issues and uncertainty in major export markets may affect demand and yarn realisations. The Company earns and spends foreign exchange (foreign exchange expenditure of Rs. 4,71,45,463 during the year), so both the demand side and input side are exposed.

risks.risk: Input-cost inflation in power, labour, finance and compliance costs
risks.note: The Company states that increasing power, labour, finance and compliance costs may exert pressure on operating margins and working-capital requirements, and that fluctuations in these inputs may reduce the competitiveness of spinning units. Spinning is power-intensive; the only stated mitigation is a strict control system to monitor day-to-day power consumption, with no captive generation or energy capex disclosed.

risks.risk: Competition from domestic mills, overseas suppliers and man-made fibres
risks.note: MD&A states that competition from domestic manufacturers, overseas suppliers and man-made fibres may affect capacity utilisation, market share and product realisations, and that competition from other cotton-producing countries and alternative fibres may pressure export volumes and product margins. Commodity cotton yarn offers little product differentiation, so utilisation and realisation are set largely by the market.

The Company is engaged in manufacturing of only one product, cotton yarn, and hence reports a single segment; all capacity sits in one unit at Haripar, Tal. Kalavad, Dist. Jamnagar, Gujarat, with an aggregate installed capacity of 39,648 spindles, and there are no subsidiaries, joint ventures or associates. There is no product, geographic or entity diversification to absorb a cotton-cycle downturn or a disruption at the single site, and the Company incurred no research and development expenditure and imported no technology during the year.

risks.risk: Scale of promoter-linked related-party trade in the same line of business
risks.note: Two ordinary resolutions seek omnibus approval for material related party transactions of up to Rs. 100 crore each for FY 2026-27, with Haripriya Spinning Mill Private Limited and Murlidhar Worldtrade Private Limited - both cotton-yarn manufacturers in which the promoters and promoter group indirectly hold substantial shareholding. The Murlidhar proposal alone equals 47.27% of the listed entity's annual consolidated turnover for the immediately preceding financial year and 210.28% of that related party's own turnover. All executive directors, promoters and the entire promoter group are interested and must abstain from voting, so pricing and volume discipline rests on the arm's-length representation and Audit Committee review rather than on independent counterparties.

The Secretarial Audit Report (Form MR-3) records that two e-forms (MGT-15 and DIR-12) were filed late with additional fees, that the outcome of the 6 November 2025 Board meeting was uploaded 26 minutes beyond the three-hour Regulation 30 deadline, and that AGM voting results were submitted one day late, for which BSE imposed and the Company paid a penalty of Rs. 10,000 under Regulation 44(3). A separate FY 2024-25 fine over an allegedly modified audit report led BSE to freeze the promoters' demat accounts until the fine was waived and de-freezing directed during FY 2025-26 - a reminder that compliance slips at this company have previously escalated to promoter-shareholding consequences.
